issues.failure_explanation: Theorem CPFBi needs several hypotheses: bi-density of D and (λ0−K)D, a norm derivative V'(0+)=K on D, and local bi-equicontinuity of {V(t)^m} uniformly in m. issues.failure_explanation: Theorem ha with complex coefficients requires analytic contraction semigroups. Koopman–Lie semigroups e^{tK_i}g = g∘σ_i are composition (shift-type) semigroups on C_b(Ω); the paper's own example shows they are not even strongly continuous, so they are not analytic, and e^{αtK_i} with complex α is undefined on C_b(Ω). The algorithms evaluate the flows at complex times, producing complex states outside Ω ⊂ R^N, where g ∈ C_b(Ω) and Proposition Frank do not apply. The remark's claim that the proof is 'algebraic' is contradicted by the outlined norm estimates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: has 7 terms and is of order 4, where $a= 0.324396 + 0.134586 i$.

issues.failure_explanation: Order raising by the triple jump requires 2a^{p+1}+(1−2a)^{p+1}=0, i.e. a = 1/(2 − 2^{1/(p+1)}ω) with ω^{p+1}=1. For k=1 the stated formula gives a_1 = 1/(1+2^{1/3}e^{−iπ/3}) ≈ 0.4237+0.2836i, which gives 2a^3+(1−2a)^3 ≈ −0.196+0.403i ≠ 0, so W_[1] is only order 2. The quoted numerical a = 0.324396+0.134586i equals 1/(2+2^{1/3}e^{−iπ/3}), which corresponds to a denominator 2^{1/(2k+1)}+2e^{πi/(2k+1)}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula by a_k = e^{πi/(2k+1)}/(2^{1/(2k+1)} + 2e^{πi/(2k+1)}), consistent with the given numbers.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's general statement (order 2k+2 for the defined W_[k]) is false as written.
issues.title: Stated coefficient formula a_k for triple-jump scheme does not give order 2k+2
issues.why_classification: It is a one-formula local correction; the numbers, order claims and scheme survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\mathcal{K}_{i}g(x)=\frac{\partial g}{\partial x_{i}}(x)\cdot {F}_{i}(x)$ generates the semigroup
where $\Omega$ is assumed closed

issues.failure_explanation: Only the full system is assumed to have unique global solutions in Ω, but the scheme needs global frozen flows that keep Ω invariant. Counterexample 1: F=(−y,x) on the closed unit disk has a global rotation flow in Ω, but the frozen flow (x_1 − t x_2, x_2) leaves Ω, so e^{tK_1}g is undefined for g∈C_b(Ω). Counterexample 2: F=(x^2y, −xy^2) has xy conserved and global solutions, yet the frozen u'=u^2y blows up at t=1/(xy).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that each frozen 1D problem is uniquely and globally solvable with Ω invariant under every sub-flow (true for the paper's examples), and narrow the stated scope accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The splitting operators and algorithms (Remarks remApp and rem324, Section 4) are ill-defined for part of the advertised class of uniquely solvable IVPs.
issues.title: Sub-flows e^{tK_i} assumed to exist globally and preserve Ω, not implied by the hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The added hypothesis is simple, but it narrows the advertised scope of 'uniquely solvable' nonlinear IVPs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This trend confirms that increasing the number of iterations improves the accuracy of the approximation

issues.failure_explanation: A local tolerance of 1e-16 does not guarantee global reference accuracy at the 1e-11 to 1e-13 level being compared.
